Bangladesh: Diamond World MD Dilip Kumar Agarwala arrested in alleged money-laundering case Dhaka Metropolitan Police arrested prominent businessman Dilip Kumar Agarwala over allegations of money laundering involving BDT 678 crore through gold and diamond smuggling. He is facing multiple legal cases currently being investigated by the Criminal Investigation Department. ANI | Updated: 19-10-2026 22:28 IST | Created: 19-10-2026 22:28 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police has arrested prominent businessman Dilip Kumar Agarwala over allegations of money laundering. Speaking to ANI over the phone, Md Shafiqul Islam, Additional Commissioner (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police, stated, "Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Detective Branch has arrested Dilip Kumar Agarwala in connection with an ongoing money laundering case being investigated by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID)." In November 2025, the CID filed a case against Dilip Kumar Agarwala over allegations of laundering BDT 678 crore through gold and diamond smuggling. Dilip Kumar Agarwala is a well-known businessman in Bangladesh and the owner and managing director of Diamond World, a jewellery chain. He is facing several cases, including an ongoing money laundering case being investigated by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID). Further details are awaited. (ANI)

item.title: French PM orders partial curfews as "ultra-left groups" fuel violent protests

item.content:encoded:
French PM orders partial curfews as "ultra-left groups" fuel violent protests French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has instructed regional authorities to impose “partial curfews” in selected urban areas on Monday evening as the nation grapples with two consecutive days of violent disturbances fuelled by "ultra-left groups", resulting in municipal town halls being burnt down and hundreds of businesses being looted, France 24 reported. ANI | Updated: 19-10-2026 22:18 IST | Created: 19-10-2026 22:18 IST

A person walks as flames rise during civil unrest, the day after a national day of demonstrations against the cost of living and rising fuel prices, in Paris, France (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has instructed regional authorities to impose “partial curfews” in selected urban areas on Monday evening as the nation grapples with two consecutive days of violent disturbances fuelled by "ultra-left groups", resulting in municipal town halls being burnt down and hundreds of businesses being looted, France 24 reported. Amid the unfolding crisis, French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday criticised security “failures” that he said led to widespread protests across the country, while rejecting the resignation of Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, France 24 reported. At least 2,400 people were arrested following the unrest, which saw town halls set on fire and hundreds of businesses looted or damaged. “The interior minister submitted his resignation to the president on Sunday,” the Élysée Palace said in a statement. “Given the necessity for continued leadership of law enforcement at this time, the president refused.” Macron had asked Nunez to “take all necessary steps to ensure transparency over the failures in planning and intelligence that led to the violence” and “put in place new operational methods for security forces” to handle the crisis, the statement added. The protests followed calls from labour unions, student organisations and activists seeking to revive the “yellow vest” movement, which emerged in 2018 to protest social injustice. Authorities estimated that Saturday's largely peaceful marches drew around 5,50,000 people, while organisers put the turnout at 8,00,000, France 24 reported. Addressing the nation on Sunday, Macron voiced public “anger” and “shame” over the rioting and looting during nationwide demonstrations against rising living costs and poor conditions in schools. He blamed much of the violence on far-left activists and accused them of attacking police and public buildings to foment chaos. “Nothing justifies it. Nothing explains it. Nothing excuses it. Tonight, we all feel anger, shame,” Macron stated. The French President also announced measures to address economic grievances, including concerns over rising fuel prices and the cost of living, while pledging firm legal action against those involved in the violence. “These protesters expressed concern about the cost of living and fuel prices, which stem from the conflict in the Persian Gulf in which France took no part, but whose consequences we bear. I fully understand their concern. It is also being expressed in several other European capitals,” Macron noted, adding that he had taken international initiatives to secure fuel and gas supplies and would travel to Gulf states to pursue those efforts, while working with fuel distributors to ensure tangible relief for consumers. Acknowledging concerns among high school and university students over their living conditions and future prospects, the President announced a structured dialogue to develop solutions with young people. “I understand our high school and university students. They have been at the heart of my political engagement for over ten years. Their voices must be heard, without preconceptions and without downplaying their difficulties,” he said. To support businesses affected by the unrest, Macron stated that Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu would chair a crisis unit to expedite assistance, while regional prefects would coordinate with local mayors to implement protective measures, including restrictions on gatherings where necessary. “Everyone must take responsibility. The country needs order, calm, not escalation,” he emphasised. Calling for firm legal action against those responsible for destruction and looting, Macron noted that the Justice Minister had instructed prosecutors to pursue cases with the “greatest firmness”. “Judicial follow-up must be exemplary. Those who destroyed must pay, those who looted must reimburse, and those who sought to bring down the Republic will have to answer for it,” he said, stressing that peaceful demonstrators should never be equated with those who destroyed, smashed and looted. The unrest included attacks on public buildings and commercial establishments in several cities, with demonstrators setting fire to a tourist information centre in Lyon, forcing their way into town halls in Marseille and Lille, and looting shops, particularly in Marseille, France 24 reported. Macron also warned against political groups exploiting street protests ahead of the presidential election scheduled in six months, urging political debate to take place peacefully. “Yes to dialogue, yes to concrete short-term responses, but no, always no, to violence of any kind. We need unity, calm, and respect,” he said. On Saturday, violent confrontations broke out between security forces and demonstrators in the capital and various regions across the country amid nationwide marches opposing escalating inflation. Multiple iconic sites were set on fire, while thieves broke into dozens of commercial outlets. Police arrested more than 2,300 people over the weekend. Meanwhile, US Under Secretary of State Jacob S. Helberg has warned of what he termed the resurgence of “far-left political terrorism”, accusing transnational networks of coordinating violence across borders and calling for action against their financing and operations. (ANI)

item.title: AI agents can pose insider security risks even without being hacked: Microsoft
item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents deployed within companies could pose significant internal security risks even without being compromised by hackers, Microsoft has warned, calling for continuous ...
item.content:encoded:
AI agents can pose insider security risks even without being hacked: Microsoft Artificial intelligence (AI) agents deployed within companies could pose significant internal security risks even without being compromised by hackers, Microsoft has warned, calling for continuous monitoring of autonomous AI systems as their use across enterprises grows. ANI | Updated: 19-10-2026 22:14 IST | Created: 19-10-2026 22:14 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Artificial intelligence (AI) agents deployed within companies could pose significant internal security risks even without being compromised by hackers, Microsoft has warned, calling for continuous monitoring of autonomous AI systems as their use across enterprises grows. In a blog post titled "Securing the agentic insider" published on Monday, Hayete Gallot, Executive Vice President, Microsoft Security, said organisations have traditionally focused on external cyber threats while placing implicit trust in AI agents deployed within their own systems. "Agents are unpredictable. They will adapt as the context changes, may not behave as intended and will collaborate and collude with other agents to reach their objectives, without needing to be compromised," Gallot stated. Microsoft warned that AI agents increasingly have access to sensitive corporate data, tools and systems, allowing them to make decisions and take actions in critical business processes. The company described these autonomous systems as "agentic insiders", highlighting the security risks arising from their growing role within organisations. "These agents are frequently overprivileged, have access to data, tools and systems and can take actions and make decisions in critical processes. They have become active participants in the enterprise," Gallot said. The warning comes as companies increasingly use AI agents to automate business operations and decision-making, raising concerns about how organisations can maintain oversight of systems capable of acting independently. Microsoft argued that securing these agents requires continuous supervision across identity, permissions, data, networks, cloud infrastructure and operating environments. "Monitoring and securing those agents must become continuous. We need to understand in real time what the agents are doing and what risks those actions create, and we need to adjust their ability to act accordingly," Gallot stated. To address these risks, Microsoft highlighted its Project Perception initiative, announced in July, which uses AI-driven security systems to help organisations detect and respond to cyber threats. The company said the same technology could be used to supervise internal AI agents through so-called Guardian Agents, which monitor their actions and intervene when risks increase. Microsoft also emphasised the need for greater transparency into how AI models make decisions, arguing that security systems must understand not only what agents are doing but also why they are taking particular actions. "Model transparency will not replace containment. It will make containment smarter and stronger," Gallot said. (ANI)

item.description: The Indian Embassy in Italy issued an advisory urging citizens to avoid crowded areas amid ongoing protests. Meanwhile, Italian PM Giorgia Meloni condemned violent clashes by criminal groups targeting ...
item.content:encoded:
Embassy advises Indian nationals in Italy to exercise caution amid protests and demonstrations The Indian Embassy in Italy issued an advisory urging citizens to avoid crowded areas amid ongoing protests. Meanwhile, Italian PM Giorgia Meloni condemned violent clashes by criminal groups targeting security forces during demonstrations, while praising peaceful protesters. ANI | Updated: 19-10-2026 20:21 IST | Created: 19-10-2026 20:21 IST

Protesters run along a street strewn with debris during a protest over the state of public services and the rising cost of living in Milan, Italy (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The Embassy of India in Italy issued an advisory on Monday directed at Indian nationals situated across the European nation, counselling them to maintain vigilance and avoid crowded areas amid ongoing protests and demonstrations. “There were protests and demonstrations last week in some Italian cities. We advise Indian nationals to exercise caution, avoid crowded areas and locations where protests are taking place and follow local news about such events,” the Embassy stated on X. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni stated on Sunday that security personnel have encountered aggression from unlawful actors who manipulate public gatherings through organised groups. “Once again, the women and men of the law enforcement forces have had to face the violence of criminals who, even through organised groups, exploit demonstrations to seek confrontation and sow chaos,” Meloni stated on X. “To all of them goes my full solidarity and sincere thanks. Because they were there to safeguard the safety of citizens, workers, merchants, and all the people who have the right to live their city without fear and without seeing it laid to waste and set ablaze by gangs of thugs. We stand with you,” she added. On Saturday, Meloni offered acknowledgement to individuals who exercised their democratic right to protest peacefully, simultaneously urging political adversaries to denounce the outbreaks of violence without reservation. “I have great respect for the thousands of people who today demonstrated peacefully, including those who took part in the mobilisation called by the CGIL, which also saw the participation of left-wing leaders. Whatever the ideas for which one demonstrates, participation is the foundation of any healthy democracy,” she said. The Italian leader noted that during disturbances in Milan, missiles were hurled at security staff, resulting in officer injuries. In Turin, authorities intercepted individuals carrying paving blocks and glass-shattering implements, whereas public disorder in Bologna necessitated the preventive shutdown of the central railway hub. “Thugs who exploit demonstrations to sow chaos, attack those who ensure security, and hold entire cities hostage,” she said. “Demonstrating is a right. Setting our cities ablaze is not,” Meloni highlighted. “I renew my request to the opposition, do not be ambiguous about this. Unequivocally condemn these acts of violence and issue a clear appeal for every mobilisation to be peaceful. In the face of scenes like these, the rejection must be unanimous. Any hesitation becomes justification. Silence is not acceptable,” Meloni emphasised. (ANI)
